annotations.annotation_text: HCE manifestation "hod" on page 98 within "The Burial of HCE": here the universal father-figure Humphrey Chimpden Earwicker appears in the context of the burial of the giant in the landscape, the archaeological mound, the Four Annalists surveying history. During this Age of Gods (transition) phase, HCE embodies the patriarch whose guilt, grandeur, and fall drive the cyclical dream forward.
sources: Glasheen, Adaline. Third Census of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/thirdcensusoffin0000glas
McHugh, Roland. The Sigla of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/siglaoffinnegans0000mchu
James Joyce Digital Archive: Finnegans Wake Notons. https://jjda.ie

annotations.annotation_text: Tavern/jury motif "pub" on page 98 ("The Burial of HCE"): the twelve customers drinking in HCE's Chapelizod pub represent public opinion, the Zodiac, and the Apostles within the burial of the giant in the landscape, the archaeological mound, the Four Annalists surveying history. During this Age of Gods (transition) phase, they judge, condemn, and demand another round — the Greek chorus of middle-class Dublin gossip.
sources: Glasheen, Adaline. Third Census of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/thirdcensusoffin0000glas
Campbell, Joseph and Robinson, Henry Morton. A Skeleton Key. https://archive.org/details/skeletonkeytofin00camp
Gordon, John. Finnegans Blog (Tavern chapters). https://johngordonfinnegan.weebly.com
